Why is compose.override.yml not used when you pass \-f? / เหตุใดจึงไม่ใช้ compose.override.yml เมื่อใส่ \-f? 

- Docker Compose only loads compose.override.yml automatically when no \-f flag is specified. Once you pass \-f, Compose switches to explicit mode and reads strictly the files listed in your command.

Why does local \+ production still publish 8085? / เหตุใด local \+ production ยัง publish พอร์ต 8085?

- Compose merges configuration files from left to right and combines ports lists rather than replacing them. Since compose.production.yml does not explicitly reset or remove the ports defined by compose.local.yml, port 8085 remains published.

Local versus server — what changes for gacha.test on a VM or a public VPS? / ในเครื่องกับบนเซิร์ฟเวอร์ต่างกันอย่างไร:  
**Name Resolution (Name → IP):**

* **Laptop:** Uses the local hosts file (127.0.0.1 gacha.test).  
* **VM:** Uses the **laptop's** hosts file pointing to the VM's LAN IP (e.g., 192.168.1.50 gacha.test).  
* **Public VPS:** Uses a real domain with a public DNS A/AAAA record pointing to the server's public IP.

**NPM Admin Access (Port 81):**

* **Laptop:** Opened directly via \[http\://127.0.0.1:81\](http\://127.0.0.1:81).  
* **VM & Public VPS:** Port 81 stays locked to loopback (127.0.0.1) on the server, so you must access it through an SSH tunnel (ssh \-L 8181:127.0.0.1:81 user@SERVER) and open http\://localhost:8181.

**Firewall & HTTPS:**

* **Laptop & VM:** Uses plain http\:// (no SSL certificate for .test).  
* **Public VPS:** Only ports 80, 443, and SSH are opened in the firewall (ports 3000, 5432, and 81 stay private/closed), and you request a free Let's Encrypt SSL certificate in NPM to enable https\://.

## 03 — CORS experiment with Docker Compose / ทดลอง CORS ด้วย Docker Compose

- Show ps for local \+ cors (app 127.0.0.1:8085, db, tester 127.0.0.1:5500).  
- Show each stage below with your own screenshot, terminal output or log line.

| Stage | What you did | Evidence (screenshot / output) | Result |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Same origin | http\://localhost:8085/visual/ → Connect |  | All passed,  Both the page and API share the exact same origin  |
| Blocked | http\://localhost:5500 → API http\://localhost:8085, CORS\_ORIGINS empty | tester ✕ \+ Console line | Blocked by browser  |
| Server still answered | curl.exe \-i \-H "Origin: http\://localhost:5500" http\://localhost:8085/health | status \+ (no) Access-Control-Allow-Origin | Server returned HTTP/1.1 200 OK as normal, without an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. |
| App log | docker compose ... logs app | CORS: page origin … is not in CORS\_ORIGINS … line | Logged warning: CORS: page origin http\://localhost:5500 is not in CORS\_ORIGINS (empty) |
| restart | edit .env, restart app, exec app printenv CORS\_ORIGINS | printenv output | Empty output — restart does not reload .env, so the container kept the old empty value. |
| up \-d | up \-d \--wait app, exec app printenv CORS\_ORIGINS | printenv output \+ curl header | Printed http\://localhost:5500 and curl returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http\://localhost:5500 |
| Allowed | reload http\://localhost:5500 → Connect, Recharge, Draw | tester ✓ screenshot | Passed (Cross-origin and allowed ✓) — All nodes turned green and Recharge/Draw succeeded. |
| Preflight | curl.exe \-i \-X OPTIONS http\://localhost:8085/api/draw ... | status \+ Access-Control-Allow-\* headers | Returned HTTP/1.1 204 No Content with Access-Control-Allow-Origin |
| 127.0.0.1 trap | http\://127.0.0.1:5500 → Connect | tester warning \+ app log line | Blocked (✕ CORS) — \[http\://127.0.0.1:5500\](http\://127.0.0.1:5500) is a different origin from http\://localhost:5500 |
| Through the proxy (optional) | http\://gacha.test/backend/visual/ → Connect | tester note | Passed (Same-origin) — Both page and API are served under \[http\://gacha.test\](http\://gacha.test), so no CORS is needed. |

Why did restart not apply CORS\_ORIGINS? / เหตุใด restart จึงไม่ใช้ค่า CORS\_ORIGINS ใหม่?

- Docker compose restart only restarts the process inside the existing container whose environment variables were fixed when it was created; up \-d is required for Compose to detect the .env change and recreate the container.

Why are http\://127.0.0.1:5500 and http\://localhost:5500 different origins? / เหตุใดสองค่านี้จึงเป็นคนละ origin?

- A web origin is defined strictly by scheme \+ host \+ port; even though both resolve to the local machine, the browser compares the host strings literally and treats 127.0.0.1 and localhost as two distinct origins. 

Why does the proxy make the page and the API same-origin, so no CORS is needed? (one sentence) / เหตุใด proxy ทำให้หน้าเว็บกับ API เป็น origin เดียวกันจึงไม่ต้องใช้ CORS (หนึ่งประโยค):

- Because the reverse proxy serves both the frontend page and the backend API under the exact same scheme, host, and port (\[http\://gacha.test\](http\://gacha.test)), the browser treats them as same-origin and skips CORS enforcement.

## Diagnosis and reflection / วิเคราะห์ปัญหาและสะท้อนผล

Symptom → hypothesis → check → fix / อาการ → สมมติฐาน → การตรวจ → วิธีแก้:

- **Symptom:** Running curl.exe \-v \[http\://gacha.test/backend/health\](http\://gacha.test/backend/health) on Windows still connected to 127.0.0.1:80 instead of the Ubuntu VM (172.18.94.76).  
- **Hypothesis:** The Windows hosts file still mapped gacha.test to 127.0.0.1 or the local DNS resolver cache held the stale entry.  
- **Check:** Verified via curl.exe \-v output showing \* Trying 127.0.0.1:80... and inspected C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\etc\\hosts.  
- **Fix:** Updated the Windows hosts file to 172.18.94.76 gacha.test, flushed the DNS cache with ipconfig /flushdns, and re-verified with curl.exe \-v showing \* Trying 172.18.94.76:80... and HTTP/1.1 200 OK.


Why does production publish no app or database ports, and what does the reverse proxy do instead? / เหตุใด production จึงไม่ publish พอร์ต app และฐานข้อมูล และ reverse proxy ทำหน้าที่อะไรแทน?

- **no ports are published:** For security—it prevents external users from directly accessing the database (5432) or the backend app (3000), reducing the risk of attacks or data leaks.  
- **What the Reverse Proxy (NPM) does instead:** It acts as the single "front door" on standard web ports (80 and 443). It checks the domain name, handles HTTPS, and forwards requests over the private Docker network so app and db only talk internally.


  
How did NPM decide which proxy host and which location answered http\://gacha.test/backend/test? / NPM เลือก Proxy Host และ location สำหรับ URL นี้อย่างไร?

- **Choosing the Proxy Host:** NPM reads the domain name from the request (Host: gacha.test) and matches it with our configured Proxy Host (localhost, gacha.test).  
- **Choosing the Location:** NPM matches the URL path (/backend/test) with our /backend/ Custom Location. It then runs the rewrite rule (rewrite ^/backend/(.\*)\$ /\$1 break;) to remove /backend, leaving /test, and forwards it to app:3000/test.


  
What changed between your laptop and the Ubuntu VM, and what operational work still belongs to the developer? / สิ่งใดเปลี่ยนระหว่างแล็ปท็อปกับ Ubuntu VM และผู้พัฒนายังต้องดูแลงานระบบอะไร?

- The app moved from running locally (127.0.0.1) to running on the Ubuntu VM's IP (172.18.94.76).  
- A firewall (ufw) now blocks unnecessary ports, allowing only 22 (SSH), 80, and 443\.  
- The NPM admin panel (port 81\) is locked to localhost inside the VM, requiring an SSH tunnel to access.  
- Database data (gacha-6788011\_pgdata) is stored separately inside the VM's disk, isolated from the laptop.

**Operational work still belonging to the developer:** Keeping Ubuntu updated with security patches, managing firewall rules and .env secrets, backing up the database volume, renewing HTTPS certificates, and checking container logs when issues occur.
